question:
Based on the situation in the sentence, select the most appropriate idiom for the underlined segment.

After the Pandemic, his business crumbled and __he is in a difficult situation__.
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **"Be in a tight corner"** means to be in a difficult situation from which it is hard to escape. (मुश्किल स्थिति में होना)

 
 
• **Example: **After losing his job, he found himself** in a tight corner** financially.
 
• **Example:** As a group of small shopkeepers in Lincoln, we are** in a really difficult situation.**
 
 

Therefore, the correct one word substitution for the given phrase is **"Be in a tight corner."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Bolt from the blue **(अचानक से कुछ होना): Something unexpected and surprising.

 
 
• **Example:** The news of his resignation came as **a bolt from the blue.**
 
 
 
• **Give a cold shoulder **(अनदेखा करना): To ignore someone deliberately.
 
 
• **Example: **She gave him **a cold shoulder **when he tried to talk to her.
 
 
 
• **Pull the last straw** (अंतिम बूँद): A final problem in a series of problems that finally makes you give up.
 
 
• **Example:** When he lost his job, it was the** last straw **for him.
